# PRIVATE CREDIT INVESTMENT MEMORANDUM

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**Date of Agreement:** September 21, 2022

**Borrower/Company Overview:** Sitio Royalties Operating Partnership, LP, a Delaware limited partnership specializing in royalty interests

**Transaction Description:** Third Amendment to Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement among Sitio Royalties Operating Partnership, LP (borrower), multiple guarantor entities, Bank of America N.A. (administrative agent), and various lenders including Barclays Bank PLC, Capital One N.A., Fifth Third Bank N.A., KeyBank N.A., Citibank N.A., Royal Bank of Canada, Credit Suisse AG, and Comerica Bank.

**Purpose of Financing:** The amendment facilitates the issuance of $450 million in 2026 Senior Notes, with proceeds being used to refinance 100% of the existing Bridge Loan Debt. The transaction involves modifications to an existing credit facility originally established on June 7, 2022.

**Company Background:** Based on available information, Sitio Royalties operates as a royalty partnership focused on oil and gas royalty interests, with multiple subsidiary entities serving as guarantors including various limited partnerships and LLCs related to energy operations in regions such as Marcellus and Eagle Ford.

## INVESTMENT HIGHLIGHTS & RISKS

**Key Strengths/Credit Positives:**
• Strong institutional lender syndicate including major banks (Bank of America, Barclays, Citibank, Royal Bank of Canada)
• Multiple subsidiary guarantors providing additional credit support and structural protection
• Successful refinancing execution demonstrates market access and debt management capability
• Borrowing base structure typical for energy/royalty companies provides asset-backed security
• Complete payoff of bridge financing reduces refinancing risk and likely improves cost of capital

**Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:**
• Energy sector exposure creates commodity price volatility risk
• Complex multi-entity structure with numerous guarantors may complicate covenant monitoring
• Borrowing base deficiency provisions indicate potential liquidity constraints during commodity downturns
• Limited financial detail available in amendment document restricts comprehensive credit assessment
• Multiple amendments to original credit agreement may indicate evolving credit conditions
